judge_reasoning: The model incorrectly concludes the puzzle is unsolvable. Its core rules claims are flawed: (1) it misunderstands that an activated/triggered ability already on the stack resolves independently of whether its source (Saheeli) is destroyed afterward, so killing Saheeli after her -2 activation doesn't undo the copy effect; (2) it claims the opponent can safely remove 3 Walking Ballista counters, but with 2 damage already marked from Shock, a second counter removal kills Ballista immediately via state-based actions, capping total safe pre-combat Ballista damage output at 2 — insufficient to kill Saheeli at 3 loyalty before her second activation resolves. The official solution is mechanically sound and achieves exactly lethal damage (4 damage to an opponent at 4 life) against optimal blocking. The model fails to find or validate the correct winning line.
model_solution:
This puzzle has no winning line under the stated rules and requirement that the opponent act optimally.

The critical issue is that Walking Ballista needs only **one** counter to disrupt the Felidar Guardian combo after Saheeli has already used −2:

1. Felidar Guardian blinks Saheeli, which returns with 3 loyalty.
2. Saheeli activates −2, going to 1 loyalty.
3. Walking Ballista removes one counter and deals 1 damage to Saheeli.
4. Saheeli is put into the graveyard before the copied Guardian can blink her again, ending the loop.

Consequently, the opponent may safely spend three Ballista counters while retaining one for the combo. For example, against the apparent intended line—copy Reckless Fireweaver, kill Winding Constrictor with Harnessed Lightning, create a Thopter, cast Shock, then attack—the opponent can spend three counters to kill Spell Queller and retain the resulting 1/1 Ballista as a blocker. It blocks Whirler Virtuoso, leaving only the two 1/3 Fireweavers to deal combat damage. The opponent takes only 8 total and survives.

The same one-counter interaction lets the opponent kill a Fireweaver or Saheeli while still retaining enough disruption against every Felidar line. Therefore no line can guarantee lethal damage against all legal opponent responses.
